_comment: Filinq capability matrix. Authored here; the cross-product index in market-intelligence is generated from it. Built by a lane generator; see the PR body for method, sources and the split of row origins.
category: Document services for the Dutch public sector, run inside Nextcloud: taking documents in (intake, scanning, OCR, classification), finding and removing personal data before disclosure (anonymisation and redaction under the Woo and the AVG, with legal grounds and publication consent), producing documents from templates in the house style, signing them, and keeping them in a state fit for the record. The research anchors it as the anonymisation app for Woo disclosure (intelligence apps.anonymization_primary_app), so its sharpest competitors are the Woo redaction products (ZyLAB ONE, xxllnc Anonimiseren); on generation it meets the government document-creation incumbents (SmartDocuments, Xential), on signing the Dutch e-signature services (ValidSign), on intake the open-source document archivers (Paperless-ngx), and across all of it the zaaksysteem and DMS suites (Decos JOIN, BCT Corsa). Case handling itself is dossiq's, publication is opencatalogi's, and the archiving process with sign-off is openregister's (decision D7), so filinq is often the provider behind another app's row. Correct this paragraph if the positioning is wrong; everything below follows from it.
